01_markdown_what_i_did: Followed the diagnose-then-fix workflow from the brief.
**Root cause confirmed as D1** (short-read on the byte-mode named pipe) — via code analysis plus a deterministic simulation, since I can't run the live pipe from the sandbox.
The pipe path is the only one that reassembles text from bytes.
In [`pipe_listener.py`](src/pipe_listener.py) the payload was read with a **single** `ReadFile(pipe, length)`.

Windows `PIPE_TYPE_BYTE` pipes don't guarantee one `ReadFile` returns all requested bytes — for longer agent responses the payload arrives fragmented, so the single read returned a **truncated prefix** (tail sentences vanish), or a cut mid-UTF-8-sequence made `decode()` raise and the broad `except` dropped the **whole** message.
The hotkey path never touches the pipe, which is exactly why it never dropped anything.
My simulation with a ≤5-byte-per-call fake `ReadFile`: old single read returned 5 of 102 bytes; new `_read_exactly` returns all 102, and mid-stream EOF raises a clean `IOError`.

10_splitting_blockquote: Read it — and I can already see the likely culprit.
The skill's ongoing-mode instructions do say "full response text" (lines 22, 33–36), but **line 42** undercuts them:
> "Don't call `speak` with markdown formatting, code blocks, or special characters — send clean readable text."
That's vague enough to license exactly what you saw: a model can read "send clean readable text" as "send a trimmed/cleaned subset," and there's **no explicit rule forbidding partial sends**.
Combined, it invites the divergence R1 was meant to prevent — full text to chat, a reduced version to `speak()`.

So the durable fix is a SKILL.md revision that makes it unambiguous: send the **entire** response verbatim — every sentence, no summarizing, no excerpting, no omissions — and reframe the formatting note so it can't be read as permission to change the words.
